To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the density of deep traps in GaAs crystals decreases with decreased As content of the melt and, as a consequence, the depletion layer width of Schottky diode detectors based on GaAs can be increased by growing GaAs crystals from Ga-rich melts.
GaAs is a promising material for solar neutrinos detection and that the EL2 traps are not a serious obstacle in this application.

1) GaAs crystals grown from melts with As compositions below 43% exhibit high resistivities, 2) the density of EL centers decreases with the As composition of the melts very gradually, 3) GaAs crystals can be grown with a low density of the EL2 donors (about 1014 cm-3), 4) the density of deep levels in GaAs is not a serious problem in terms of its impact on the depletion width in GaAs radiation detectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of semi-insulating GaAss grown by the liquid encapsulated Czohralski technique as a material for high energy radiation detectors.
the evaluation of GaAs as the material for solar neutrinos detectors.
the evaluation of GaAs crystals as a possible material of radiation detectors with a large active volume, such as those used for solar neutrino experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EL2-related deep levels do not pose a major problem for the development of GaAs-based solar neutrino detectors with active layer thicknesses up to several millimeters.
the use of GaAs as an alternative material to Si in solar neutrino detectors is not justified.
the use of GaAs as material for radiation detectors is limited due to a relatively high density of deep donors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GaAs crystals grown from Ga-rich melts with As composition above 43% are not suitable for radiation detection applications due to the high density of deep donors.

the density of midgap traps in GaAs crystals grown from Ga-rich melts is low enough to make this material attractive for radiation detection applications, however, it is not as low as to make GaAs a perfect material for such applications.
the GaAs material with a high active volume is a promising material for solar neutrinos detectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EL2 donors are the most serious obstacle to achieving a large depletion layer width in semi-insulating GaAssolar cells.
the density of deep traps in GaAs can be decreased by about two orders of magnitude by using a Ga-rich melt and post-growth annealing.
GaAs is a promising material for solar neutrinos detectors with a large active layer thickness.
